texts.preamble: Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 In The Court Of Mayuri Singh Presiding Officer : Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, East District : Karkardooma Courts Delhi Cnr No.: Dlet01-000094-2018 Macp No.188/19 Kriti Kishore @ Krity Kishore Vs. Nand Kishore & Ors . In the matter of : Kriti Kishore & Krity Kishore (Injured) D/o Sh. Naval Kishore R/o Flat No. 802, Arawali Apartment, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. -Petiti Versus 1. Nand Kishore (Driver-cum-owner of Hydra Crane No. Hr-55V-4780 and owner of Hydra Crane No. Hr-99Xbt-4138) S/o Sh. Kashi Nath R/o F-107, Village Ghazipur, Delhi. 2. Satender Singh Yadav (Driver of Hydra Crane No. Hr-99Xbt-4138) S/o Sh. Ram Nath R/o F-107, Village Ghazipur, Delhi. 3.Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. (Insurer of Vehicle No. Hr- 55V-4780) Fai Building 10, Shaeed Jeet Singh Marg, Qutub Institutional Area, New Delhi. -Respondents Date of institution : 05.01.2018 Date of reserve of order : Not reserved Date of Award : 19.07.2024 Awar D 1.
texts.facts: By this award, the claim petition bearing MACP No.188/19 seeking compensation under Sections 166 (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the accident, based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) would be decided. 2. Briefly stated facts as per the FIR are that on 29.08.2017 at about 6:50 pm, the petitioner was coming back to her house at Arawali Apartment, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. from her office via National Highway-24, Ghazipur, Delhi on her scooty bearing registration No DL-7SBD-9244. It is further stated that the petitioner took turn from flyover circle of Ghazipur Murga Mandi towards EDM Mall, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, U.P. and at that time, two hydra cranes bearing registration No. Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 1 HR-55V-4780 and HR-99XBT-4138 were carrying a big stone without following the public safety and safeguards or blocking of the road there. While the petitioner passed by therefrom, one crane bearing registration No HR-55V-4780 came over the petitioner, as a result of which, petitioner fell down on road alongside her scooty and weight loading part of the crane fell down over the right hand of the petitioner and smashed her right hand. FIR bearing no. 313/17 PS- Ghazipur, was registered in connection with the accident. 3. In response to the notice of the petition, all the respondents appeared and filed their replies / written statements. 3(i). In the joint written statement filed by respondent Nos. 1 & 2 (in the capacity of the owner and driver respectively of Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-99XBT-4138), they have asserted that no accident has even been committed by the respondent No.2 at any point of time with Crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 and police has falsely implicated the respondent No. 1 & 2 in the present matter. It is further averred that said vehicle is not involved in the alleged accident. It is further asserted that police officials of PS Ghazipur have obtained the signatures of the respondents on blank papers in the police station. It is further averred that the investigating officer has not conducted a fair investigation. It is further stated that respondents are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners. It is further stated that the respondent No. 2 had a valid driving licence. In the separate written statement filed by R1 (in the capacity of the owner-cum-driver of Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-55V-4780), it is stated that no accident has been committed at any point of time with the alleged vehicle bearing No.HR-55V-4780. It is further stated that police has falsely implicated R1 and he is not liable to pay any compensation and further that the said crane was duly insured on the date of accident and having other relevant documents i.e. fitness, permit, RC etc. and further that R1 had a valid driving licence. 3(ii). Respondent No.3 / insurer has filed its written statement and has taken defence that the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. Hydra Crane bearing Registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 was not holding any valid driving licence on the date of accident for driving the class of vehicle involved in the accident. It is further stated that crane bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 was not having any valid permit and fitness certificate for use in the present case. It is stated that the permit was valid only for Haryana and the fitness was valid upto 02.03.2017, whereas the accident took place on 29.08.2017 and thus terms and conditions of the insurance policy have been willfully violated by the insured. It is further stated that owner and insurer of crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138 have not been made a party nor any document of the said vehicle has been filed in the DAR. It is further stated that as per DAR, the concrete slab slipped from HR-99XBT-4138 due to the negligence of Respondent No.2/Satender and due to the load of the slab, the other crane bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 toppled, falling on the injured and thus the negligence was solely of the crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138. It is further averred that insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55V-4780 was not responsible for the alleged accident, which was caused due to the sole negligence of the crane bearing registration No. HR-99XBT-4138. 4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 06.06.2019:- Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 2 (OPP) (iv)Relief. 5. In order to establish her claim, petitioner examined three witnesses. 5(i). Petitioner / PW1 deposed on the strength of affidavit Ex.PW1/A and deposed regarding manner of accident, injuries suffered by her and the medical expenses incurred on her treatment and relied upon the following documents:- Photocopy of driving licence and aadhar card of petitioner are Ex.PW1/1 (colly,2 sheets) (OSR) Attested copy of medical documents of the petitioner is Ex. PW1/2 (colly, 212 pages) Photocopies of academic documents of the petitioner are Ex. Computer generated salary slip of the petitioner is Ex.PW1/5 Photocopies of computer generated IRT of the assessment year 2017-18 alongwith PAN card are Ex. PW1/6 (colly, 6 sheets) PW2 Dr. Sanjeev Gambhir, Specialist Orthopedics, LBS Hospital, Khichripur, Delhi proved the disability certificate as Ex. PW2/A mentioning 93% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb. PW3, Sh. Akash Singh, Sr. Executive, Max Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi produced the treatment record of the petitioner and proved three discharge summaries of the petitioner Ex. PW3/A to Ex. PW3/C. Further, he also proved three final bills of the Max Hospital Ex.PW3/D, Ex. PW3/E and Ex. PW3/F. 19. According to her affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was first taken to Yashoda Hospital, Kaushambi Ghaizabad, and thereafter shifted to Max Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi. Her right hand elbow was operated upon and injury of the petitioner was diagnosed as crush injury right elbow with fracture, dislocation near total amputation with right distil ulna fracture with crush injury right index finger with right ILIAC wing fracture. In her affidavit attested on 31.01.2018, she stated that she could not recover and is having same problem in her right hand and further that she was on bed and her repeated dressing were being done at the hospital with no improvement shown and further that she was unable to resume her job. OPD consultation of Max hospital shows that she visited the hospital for treatment at least till 27.11.2017. The bill summary of Yashoda Hospital reflects that she was admitted there on 29.08.2017 and thereafter discharged on the same day. Further, the duplicate bill of Max Hospital shows that she was admitted to the hospital on 29.08.2017 and discharged on 15.09.2017. Further, another duplicate bill of Max Hospital shows that she was admitted on 19.09.2017 and discharged on 23.09.2017. In these circumstances, considering the nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs. 3,00,000/- to the petitioner under this head. CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 20. Thus, I deem it fit to grant a sum of Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner towards special diet. In her examination-in-chief Ex. PW1/A tendered on 30.05.2022 by way of affidavit attested on 31.01.2018, petitioner deposed that she is an MBA and at the time of accident, she was working with Parcel Now World Wide, a logistic startup and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
texts.arguments: (New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656). Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 5 12. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act. If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence. 16. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases. It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 6 and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured. The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity. What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income. All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity. In this regard, petitioner has relied on judgment of Hon'ble Bombay High Court bearing citation Royal Sundaram Alliance Company Ltd. Vs. Mr. Ajit Chandrakant Rakvi & Anr. FA No.1620 of 2012, decided on 19.03.2019. United India Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Patrica Jean Mahajan & Ors. of Supreme Court of India in Appeal (Civil) 3655-58 of 2002; and Mrs. Helen C. Rebello & Ors. Vs. Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation of Supreme Court of India decided on 18.09.1998. For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 8 doing of the driver. (DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253). Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- as attendant charges. 22. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- (30,000+50,000 + 40,000) under this head. Due to permanent disability sustained in the accident, she would not be able to get job in the same way as prior to the accident and she is unable to resume her job. During her cross-examination, she stated that she had worked for 06 months in the above-stated company prior to the accident and further that she joined her service after the accident in September 2019 in another company namely Aquagiri Processing Pvt. Ltd. Ld. Counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner could not work for 22 months due to the injuries sustained in the accident. However, this claim is not substantiated through medical record or even through the testimony of petitioner. It is an admitted case she was never thrown out of job and instead during the period of her treatment itself, the company where she was working had been shut down. Hence, there is no question of her re-joining the same job. There is nothing in the shape of medical documents to show that she was unable to take up new employment till September 2019 or that she made an effort to take up new job but due to the injuries sustained by her, she was declined a suitable job. However, considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the continuous treatment and admission in hospital and further the long period of treatment, it can reasonably be assumed that she remained unable to work for about 10 months from the date of accident. She was getting salary of Rs.39,800/- per month on the date of accident and hence, on account of loss of income, an amount of Rs. 3,98,000/- (39,800 X10) is being awarded as compensation under this head. Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 40 % has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was less than 40 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252, Rajasthan High Court). The monthly income of the petitioner on the date of accident was about Rs.39,800/-. Thus, the petitioner is entitled to compensation for the sum of Rs. 34,10,064/-[30% of (39,800x140/100x12x17=1,13,66,880/-)].Therefore, a sum of Rs.34,10,064 /- is awarded to the petitioner under this head. LOSS OF AMENITIES, DISFIGURATION, LOSS OF EXPECTATION OF LIFE & MARRIAGE PROSPECTS 27. There is no evidence led by the petitioner to suggest that the longevity of petitioner has been adversely affected due to the accident in question or that petitioner had any particular dream for future, which is shattered due to accident and there is absolutely no evidence to show any loss of expectation of life. During oral argument addressed, it was stated by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner that petitioner was about to get married at the time of accident but her marriage was postponed on account of this accident and by grace of God, eventually she got married to the same man with Kriti Kishor vs Nand Kishore on 19 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180338634/ 11 whom marriage was fixed earlier. In the totality of the facts and circumstances, even though there is no evidence to suggest that there was any loss of marriage prospects, considering that permanent disability suffered not only resulted in restricted movement of limb but also affected adversely the physical appearance further petitioner shall also not be able to do several activities, including those involving kid and adults alike and thus she will not able to enjoy life to the fullest as before, a sum of Rs. 1,50,000/- is awarded towards Loss of expectation of life and loss of marriage prospects. Petitioner is granted Rs.1,00,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.1,50,000/- for disfiguration as she suffered from near total amputation of right hand. In case titled as Gurmeet Singh vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd & Ors, MAC App 288/2021 decided on 06.10.2023, it has been held that the respondent no. 3/ insurer is entitled to recover the compensation amount paid to the claimants.
